newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in, slows won drop vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in, slows won drop vs dollar.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened in the interbank foreign exchange market to stop the local currency's drop against the U.S. unit, dealers said.
They said the central bank sold dollars as the won stood at 844.20 won. The won/dollar rate soon recovered to 842.70.
"Today's intervention appears to be designed to root out speculative buying sentiment that has survived last week's repeated interventions," said one dealer.
Central bank officials denied the bank intervened as they routinely do.
The South Korean won has been on a steep decline against the U.S. dollar due to a continued slump in its exports and the weakening Japanese yen against the U.S. unit, dealers said.
